plants.name: Hippeastrum spp.
plants.description: Towering stems carry huge trumpet-shaped blooms in glowing shades of scarlet, white and candy pink. Each flower opens wide like a festive fanfare.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly November to January). Indoors in the Northern Hemisphere, potted bulbs are timed to flower from December to February.
plants.location: Gardens in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, plus windowsills across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can bloom again year after year. After flowering, the plant needs a rest period so it can store energy for the next display.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs burst into rose-like flowers in winter. The blooms stand out against dark, leathery leaves, and they brighten gardens in the cold months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with early and mid-season varieties in full flower in December
plants.location: Mild-winter regions such as the southeastern United States, the Pacific Northwest, Japan and southern Europe
plants.funFact: Tea comes from a close relative, Camellia sinensis. Camellia japonica seeds are pressed to make a prized culinary and cosmetic oil in Japan.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A wide, umbrella-shaped canopy turns fiery orange-red when the tree flowers. Ferny leaves frame clusters of ruffled petals, each with a single white-streaked standard petal.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from about November to February in many regions
plants.location: Southern Hemisphere warm climates such as northern Australia, Brazil and Madagascar, where it is native
plants.funFact: The tree is native to Madagascar, where it is now endangered in the wild. Meanwhile it is planted as a showy shade tree throughout the tropics.
